content: This medication is used to treat constipation by increasing the bulk in your stool, which helps stimulate intestinal movement. It is essential to take this medication exactly as directed by your doctor or as per the instructions on the product packaging if you are self-treating. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. To prevent choking, always take this medication with a full glass of water or another liquid (8 ounces or 240 milliliters). For powdered forms, measure the dose as instructed on the product label, mix it thoroughly in a full glass of water or liquid, and drink it immediately. If the mixture becomes too thick, you may add more liquid. Dosage is determined based on your age, medical condition, and response to treatment. This product may interfere with the absorption of other medications. To avoid this, take it at least two hours apart from other medications. It may take one to three days for this medication to start working. For optimal results, use it regularly and at the same time(s) each day. If your condition persists, worsens, or if you experience rectal bleeding, inform your doctor promptly. Common side effects include gas or stomach cramping. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, this product must be taken with at least a full glass of liquid to prevent it from swelling in the throat, which could cause choking. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. If you experience symptoms such as difficulty breathing, chest pain, or swelling, seek immediate medical attention. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. Some products may contain inactive ingredients, such as sugar or aspartame, which could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Use caution if you have diabetes, phenylketonuria (PKU), or any condition requiring dietary restrictions. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. In case of overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Lifestyle changes, such as regular exercise, adequate water intake, and a fiber-rich diet (e.g., bran, fresh fruits, and vegetables), can help prevent or relieve constipation. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose. Different brands of this medication may have different storage requirements. Check the product packaging for specific instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
